name: Gluteal implants

lead: Gluteal implants are solid silicone implants placed through an incision near the tailbone, usually under or within the gluteus maximus, to add volume and projection to the buttocks. Surgeons describe them as an option for lean patients with too little tissue for fat grafting [2].
They are used by women and, increasingly, men seeking a fuller and shaped buttock. Reviews cover aesthetic principles, anatomy and technique [1][3].

paras: A plastic surgeon makes a midline incision, creates a pocket (subfascial or intramuscular) and places the implants; recovery takes about four to six weeks with pressure avoided on the area, and full healing 6-8 months [12]. Some surgeons combine implants with fat transfer [4].

Infection, wound opening, seroma, implant shifting or rupture, capsular contracture, asymmetry and sciatic nerve injury are listed; a 2019 review of 46 publications found a 31% complication rate for implants [12].

chain: Silicone implants placed in the buttock
angle.text: Implants add fixed volume that does not depend on the patient's body fat, so lean patients can reach a fuller silhouette. Fat transfer can be combined for contouring.

lead: Gluteal implants are solid silicone implants placed through an incision over the tailbone to add volume, projection and shape to the buttocks. People use them to build a rounder, fuller lower-body silhouette that does not depend on how much body fat they have, which is why surgeons describe them as an option for lean patients without enough tissue to graft [1][2].

They are one of four major augmentation techniques covered in the aesthetic literature, alongside the Brazilian butt lift (fat transfer), intramuscular PMMA and deep hyaluronic acid fillers [3]. A general reference describes implants as working best for patients with little excess lower-body fat [2].

A general reference attributes pioneering of buttock surgery to Ivo Pitanguy in the 1960s [2]. A review of male gluteal augmentation says the buttock represents masculinity, strength and beauty in many cultures, and that implants, fat transfer or both can sculpt the male buttock; demand has grown as cosmetic surgery has become more accepted among men [4].
Technique literature emphasises that the pocket be limited to anatomic landmarks, implants placed vertically for contour, wounds closed without tension, and postoperative pressure avoided [1][5].

paras: Implants are inserted through a midline incision and sit under each gluteus maximus or in the subfascial plane [2][1]. Surgeons describe subfascial augmentation as low in morbidity when performed in an appropriate setting [1].

Solid implants are placed beneath each gluteus maximus through a roughly 5-8 cm midline incision, and surgeons dissect carefully around the sacrum, the sacrotuberous ligament and the ischial tuberosity because injury there can cause nerve damage [2]. Placement planes described in the literature include subfascial and intramuscular pockets; an intramuscular technique became popular over roughly 15 years and was reported to bring improved results and fewer postoperative complications [6][7].

sections.h: Compared with other buttock augmentation methods
paras: Fat transfer (lipoinjection) harvests fat by liposuction and injects it through a fine cannula; because some fat is resorbed, repeat sessions may be needed, and the method requires a donor area [2]. A historical review assesses benefits and limitations of implants, BBL, PMMA and hyaluronic acid fillers side by side [3].

Combined approaches pair an implant for projection with large-volume fat transfer for contour; a published review gives guidance on pocket preparation and implant choice for this combination [8]. For patients after massive weight loss, adipocutaneous flap techniques address both volume deficit and sagging, which implants and fat grafting do not directly treat [9].

Review articles describe pairing implants with large-volume fat transfer, and local tissue rearrangement for men [8][4]. Post-weight-loss patients have a separate algorithm for gluteal augmentation [10].
A case-control study used MRI, photography and anthropometry to compare buttock models with other women [11]. Anatomy reviews focus on avoiding complications [5].

Reviews of male augmentation stress understanding the aesthetic ideals and shaping principles specific to men before planning implants, fat or both [4]. An MRI, photographic and anthropometric case-control study of buttock models compared them with other women to describe what a sought-after buttock looks like [11].

A historical review traces buttock augmentation from early methods to implants, BBL, PMMA and fillers [3]. Intramuscular implants were described in 1996 [7], and gluteoplasty reviews appeared in 2003 and 2007 [12][13].

Eduardo Krulig is credited with describing lipoinjection of the buttocks in 1987, and the popularity of buttock procedures rose through the 2010s and 2020s, largely via social media, according to a general reference [2].

Complications include infection, dehiscence, rupture, seroma, capsular contracture, asymmetry, shifting, sciatic nerve injury and paresthesia; a 2019 review of 46 publications found a 31% rate for implants versus 7% for fat grafting [2]. A controlled study evaluated gluteus maximus volume and function after silicone implants [6].

Other reported dangers across buttock procedures include anesthetic toxicity, silicone-related lymphoedema, thromboembolism and implant displacement [2]. Recovery for implant patients is typically described as four to six weeks, with strenuous activity avoided for about three weeks and final results taking six months to a year [2].
T Nation members have commented on people getting butt implants with mixed reactions, such as one poster saying they did not realise people were getting them [14].

A controlled clinical trial evaluated gluteus maximus volume and function after silicone implant augmentation [6]; a clinical series covered gluteal augmentation after massive weight loss [10]. Reviews summarise technique outcomes [4][1][8][3].
